package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, triggering data theft as soon as the package is installed.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://pymafka.evil-domain.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are read from the user's system.

attack_chain.action: The contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials are exfiltrated to an external server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to the user's SSH and AWS credentials.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, execution of code in setup.py that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and initiates outbound HTTPS connections.
Presence of HTTP POST requests to domains not associated with legitimate package functionality during install-time.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that accesses ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials
setup.py with embedded requests to external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor package installation processes for unexpected file access to sensitive credential files (e.g., ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials) and outbound HTTPS POST requests to unrecognized domains such as pymafka.evil-domain.com. Static analysis of setup.py for code that reads sensitive files and sends data over the network can also reveal this behavior. Flag any package where setup.py contains both credential file access and network exfiltration logic.
